entries.title: HSBC Egypt alerts
entries.summary: Reads HSBC Egypt alert mails and text messages into Money as transactions, each with the balance it prints, and a message that only prints a balance as a balance check.
entries.author: BrainDog

versions.notes: Nothing it reads or writes changed. Two like movements a day apart stay two when each prints its own balance or its own InstaPay reference, and the mail and the text of one movement stay one. A balance can come back to a figure it printed before, as when one sum is withdrawn, paid back in and withdrawn again on the same day: the second withdrawal is then held as a repeat that names the one it looks like, and “It is a second one” files it.

Each amount a message prints without a currency is read in its account's own currency, never in pounds sterling. Two like movements a day apart stay two when each prints its own balance or its own InstaPay reference, and the mail and the text of one movement stay one. A question about digits no account holds now says whether it is a card or an account.
A card charge and an InstaPay transfer keep the shop or the person as the bank wrote it, in a new Paid to or from field, so the same payee is recognised however it is spelled.
Nothing it reads or writes changed. The add-on has a title of its own now, and each version says what it changed in a line like this one.

entries.title: Card alerts
entries.summary: Reads a card alert that names the card's last four digits into Money as a transaction, forwarded by mail or posted as a text message.
entries.author: BrainDog

versions.notes: An alert that prints no currency is read in its card's own currency. A card alert is only ever matched to a card, never to an account whose digits end alike, and a question about digits no card holds says it is a card.
Each alert keeps the shop or the sender as the alert names it, in a new Paid to or from field, so the same payee is recognised however it is spelled.
Nothing it reads or writes changed. Each version says what it changed in a line like this one.

entries.title: Count the cash
entries.summary: Write down what is actually in a cash box or an account, and the record keeps it as a balance check and writes the difference from what it thought was there into the ledger.
entries.author: BrainDog

rules: Write the difference of each count

versions.notes: A count in another currency than its account now says so on the count, under What happened: which two currencies, and to count in the account's currency. Before, the reason went to the run's log alone, so the count stood with no difference and no word. Nothing else changed: still no balance check and no difference are written for such a count.

rules: Write the difference of each count

versions.notes: A count that was not compared because its account holds an entry in another currency now says which balance to type: the balance its bank or statement shows, not the cash in the box, then count again. Before, it said to type the account's balance, which read as the cash just counted, and a box typed that way agrees with the next count and never shows the gap. Nothing else changed: still no balance check and no difference are written for such a count.

rules: Write the difference of each count

versions.notes: A count that was not compared because its account holds an entry in another currency now says the way out under What happened: type the account's balance, then count again. Before, it said only that it was not compared, and the account went on reading as uncounted. Nothing else changed: still no balance check and no difference are written for such a count.

rules: Write the difference of each count

versions.notes: An account that holds a cleared entry in another currency since it was last stated is no longer compared. The count is kept and says so under What happened, and no balance check and no difference are written, where before the entry was left out and a difference equal to it could be filed. An account whose entries are all in one currency is counted as before.

rules: Write the difference of each count

entries.summary: Reads the Ledger for a charge made twice and a payment that repeats, and asks you once about each. Charged twice stops asking about a payee whose last three answers were Both real, and Looks like it repeats switches itself off after three No's in a row.

versions.notes: Charged twice and Looks like it repeats keep a short number that is part of a shop's name. Studio 54 Cafe was read as Studio, so two shops that start alike were one payee. A number of one or two digits now stays in the name unless it is the day of a date, so SPOTIFY 12 OCT, SPOTIFY 12OCT and SPOTIFY OCT 12 are all Spotify. A card number in groups, as in CARD 1234 5678 NETFLIX, is cut whole.
